disclaimer: Entirely fictional, nonconfidential demonstration data. No real operator, asset, incident, or operating instruction is represented. Times are anchored to the synthetic replay epoch, not live operations. Scenario applicability is private retrieval routing metadata and is not diagnostic evidence.

records.title: Pressure anomaly desk assessment and bounded inspection planning
records.body: Fictional, nonconfidential procedure. The desk assessment uses pressure timing, persistence, coverage and paired taps to scope uncertainty before any inspection recommendation. Trunk P1, Branch A P2 and Branch B P3 each have ST1 through ST4 with A/B pressure taps; ST1/ST3 share gateway-<segment>-0 and ST2/ST4 share gateway-<segment>-1. Agreement within a shared gateway is not independent telemetry corroboration. A bounded inspection area requires support from distinct stations and gateways, with exclusions and missing observers recorded. Operating logs and maintenance history are context, not proof of an integrity condition. Incomplete log coverage cannot establish that no operation occurred. Physical intervention remains subject to operator authorization.

records.title: Pressure-setpoint change review index
records.body: Fictional, nonconfidential desk-review index. Explicit operation-history reference: OP-VALVE-001, upstream valve pressure-setpoint change at synthetic second 90. The event entry contains execution timing and affected segments. The associated historical comparison is INC-TRANSIENT-001. A logged operation can motivate comparison of actual pressure histories on P1, P2 and P3 across gateway-P1-0/1, gateway-P2-0/1 and gateway-P3-0/1; this index contains no measured current response and cannot settle whether another condition coexists.

records.title: P1-ST2-A calibration release, withdrawn revision
records.body: Fictional, nonconfidential withdrawn maintenance note. The initial bench release recorded P1-ST2-A as within tolerance and recommended unrestricted use. A subsequent repeatability check contradicted that release; revision 2 MAINT-CAL-P1-002 replaces this note. This old bench result describes neither current pressure nor the health of the other tap at ST2.

records.title: P1-ST2-A calibration repeatability exception
records.body: Fictional, nonconfidential maintenance note. Repeat calibration of P1-ST2-A showed warm-up dependent positive offset drift after the initial acceptable bench result. The transmitter remains in observation pending replacement; no correction has been applied to replay values. P1-ST2-B was not adjusted. Both taps share gateway-P1-1, so a paired comparison alone does not exclude gateway effects. The note supports a sensor-quality investigation but supplies no current physical diagnosis.

records.title: Proposed P1-ST2-A return to service
records.body: Fictional, nonconfidential unsigned proposal. A return-to-service release for P1-ST2-A was drafted on the assumption that a replacement transmitter would pass calibration. The replacement and acceptance check have not been recorded. This draft is not an approved change to the revision 2 observation restriction.

records.title: Branch A ST2-A intermittent impulse investigation
records.body: Fictional, nonconfidential maintenance note. Branch A sensor P2-ST2-A intermittently produced isolated positive impulses during a connector reseat check. No corresponding impulse was logged on paired tap P2-ST2-B during that check. Connector replacement is pending; gateway-P2-1 serves both ST2 and ST4. The observation predates the current pressure window and is a possible instrumentation confounder, not an explanation for every future excursion.

records.title: Branch B ST3-A sample loss on gateway P3-0
records.body: Fictional, nonconfidential telemetry maintenance note. Intermittent sample loss was observed on the P3-ST3-A channel carried by gateway-P3-0. Investigation has not separated channel scheduling from a local transmitter fault. ST1 and ST3 share this gateway; the work item does not establish a gateway-wide outage or missing pressure values as zero. Current availability requires measurement from the pressure history and arrival records.

records.title: Executed upstream valve pressure-setpoint change at second 90
records.body: Fictional, nonconfidential executed operating log. At 2026-01-01T00:01:30Z (synthetic second 90), the upstream pressure-control valve setpoint was reduced from 80.0 to 79.25 bar. Execution was acknowledged at second 100 and the log became available at second 110. Hydraulic scope is Trunk P1 and downstream Branch A P2 and Branch B P3, all four stations on each segment. This entry records a commanded change, not measured pressure at the taps. Expected broad pressure response remains a hypothesis to compare against actual pre/post pressure histories from independent gateways; coincident localized behavior is not excluded.

records.title: Earlier network-wide response following a setpoint reduction
records.body: Fictional, nonconfidential historical incident report. A previous 0.75 bar upstream setpoint reduction was followed by a near-concurrent downward pressure step at multiple stations on Trunk P1, Branch A P2 and Branch B P3, spanning all six gateways. The desk review associated that earlier transient with the operating change after comparing actual histories. Its amplitudes and timing are an analogy, not a prediction or a determination of present integrity. This historical report does not establish whether a current leak or instrumentation defect is present or absent.

records.title: Incomplete telemetry restoration work order
records.body: Fictional, nonconfidential open work order. Telemetry restoration is incomplete following loss of most observers at synthetic second 90. The last desk acknowledgement identifies only the P1-ST2 A/B pair on gateway-P1-1 as reporting; the observer inventory is provisional and needs comparison with current arrivals. Coverage across other stations and independent gateways is unverified. No physical inspection result is attached. This work order describes an evidence limitation and neither confirms nor excludes an integrity event.

records.title: Operating-log coverage and missing source limitations
records.body: Fictional, nonconfidential source coverage statement. This excerpt is not a complete plant historian: third-party upstream activity, manual field actions and delayed shift entries may be absent. No contemporaneous operation entry in this excerpt explains a localized Trunk P1 pressure drop. Absence of such an entry is not evidence that no operation occurred, nor confirmation of a leak. Pressure histories, sensor-quality observations and independent gateway coverage remain necessary; unavailable logs remain an explicit uncertainty.

records.title: Later fictional inspection confirmation for Trunk P1
records.body: Fictional, nonconfidential later inspection report. A simulated inspection at second 270 documented a small fluid escape near P1 chainage 400 m, between ST2 and ST3. The report was authored at second 300 and released at second 360; no observation in this report was available at second 185. This is a later physical inspection account, not an authoritative detector label and not evidence available to an earlier desk assessment.
